body:
Apollo Global Management has set up a European private credit business with €10 billion (approximately $11.2 billion) of lending capacity, aiming to fund defense, energy and infrastructure projects across the continent.

The vehicle, called European Credit Company, will make corporate and asset-backed loans to companies, sponsors and owners of real assets, including infrastructure and real estate, the company said Monday. It will focus on performing credit in both the large and mid-market segments.

Giacomo Petrobelli is chief executive of the platform, with Christian Meissner serving as chairman. It will operate from offices in Frankfurt, Jersey, London, Luxembourg City and Milan, working alongside Apollo's wider operations.

The Abu Dhabi Investment Council anchors a group of strategic backers that also includes European insurer Athora, Japan's Norinchukin Bank, Standard Chartered and U.S. credit investor Aranda Principal Strategies.

Petrobelli framed the launch as a chance to fund Europe's long-term growth. The platform's goal, he said, is to become "a premier pan-European credit platform, focused exclusively on the region, with deep local relationships, differentiated sourcing and flexible solutions that span all credit types."

Apollo president Jim Zelter pointed to what he called a global industrial renaissance that is generating heavy financing needs, felt most sharply in Europe across the energy transition and transmission, defense, and digital and traditional infrastructure.

The new platform lands amid rapid growth in private credit. Moody's expects assets under management in the asset class to top $2 trillion in 2026 and approach $4 trillion by 2030.

Apollo's tie-up with the Abu Dhabi Investment Council follows its agreement, disclosed about a week earlier, to acquire a stake of nearly 10% in Mubadala Capital, the alternative asset management arm of Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund Mubadala Investment Co.
